title: Case report: Transplantation of human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocyte patches for ischemic cardiomyopathy.

items.referenceFact: Report the first implantation of allogeneic hiPSC-CM patches in a patient with ischemic cardiomyopathy to evaluate safety and potential efficacy.
items.generatedFact: First-in-human case report of hiPSC-CM patch transplantation for ischemic cardiomyopathy.

quotes: Based on preclinical studies, allogenic human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocyte (hiPSC-CM) patches have been proposed as a potential therapeutic candidate for heart failure. We report the implantation of allogeneic hiPSC-CM patches in a patient with ischemic cardiomyopathy (ClinicalTrials.gov, #jRCT2053190081). The patches were produced under clinical-grade conditions and displayed cardiogenic phenotypes and safety in vivo (severe immunodeficient mice) without any genetic mutations in cancer-related genes. The patches were then implanted via thoracotomy into the left ventricle epicardium of the patient under immunosuppressive agents.

quotes: Allogeneic human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocyte (hiPSC-CM) patches, produced under clinical-grade protocols, were investigated as a regenerative approach for ischemic cardiomyopathy. We report a first-in-human case in which three hiPSC-CM patches (3.3 × 10⁷ cells per patch) were implanted onto the left ventricular (LV) epicardium of a 51-year-old male with NYHA class III ischemic cardiomyopathy (baseline LV ejection fraction 30%) via thoracotomy, under intra-aortic balloon pumping (IABP) support and a three-month immunosuppressive regimen.

quotes: No lethal arrhythmias, tumor formation, or immunosuppression-related serious adverse events were detected over a one-year observation period. NYHA functional class improved from III to II at both 6 months and 1 year. Four-dimensional computed tomography demonstrated enhanced regional wall motion at the grafted sites, while ¹³N-ammonia PET imaging showed that whole-heart coronary flow reserve increased from 2.16 at 6 months to 5.30 at 1 year post-implantation. Fluorodeoxyglucose-PET revealed no evidence of tumorigenesis. These initial findings suggest the procedure was well tolerated and associated with functional recovery, although the single-patient design precludes causal inference.

quotes: No lethal arrhythmias, tumor formation, or immunosuppression-related serious adverse events were detected over a one-year observation period. NYHA functional class improved from III to II at both 6 months and 1 year. Four-dimensional computed tomography demonstrated enhanced regional wall motion at the grafted sites, while ¹³N-ammonia PET imaging showed that whole-heart coronary flow reserve increased from 2.16 at 6 months to 5.30 at 1 year post-implantation. Fluorodeoxyglucose-PET revealed no evidence of tumorigenesis. These initial findings suggest the procedure was well tolerated and associated with functional recovery, although the single-patient design precludes causal inference.
